data.command: Can you tell me about your firewall rules?

data.text:
Our firewall rules are configured using the `iptables` system. We're running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, and I've got the rules set up to allow incoming traffic on certain ports. Let me check the current rules for you...

`sudo iptables -n -L`

Okay, so here's what I see:

`Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)`

`target     prot src      dpt  user     
ACCEPT     all  anywhere     22  sshd`

`ACCEPT     tcp  anywhere     80  http`

`ACCEPT     tcp  anywhere     443  https`

`ACCEPT     all  anywhere     1234  ( custom rule for our web app )`

`DROP       all  anywhere     any`

`Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)`

`target     prot src      dpt  user     
ACCEPT     all  anywhere     22  sshd`

`ACCEPT     all  anywhere     80  http`

`ACCEPT     all  anywhere     443  https`

Simple rules, really. We're allowing SSH on port 22, HTTP on port 80, HTTPS on port 443, and a custom rule for our web app on port 1234. Everything else gets dropped.
